title: What are your Top 10 most underrated movies?

commenti.body:
1) The Boy and the Bridge (1959)

5 ratings

A film in the tradition of The Red Balloon whose child-scale perspective makes everything bigger, grander — and sometimes scarier — than reality.

2) A Moon for My Father (2019)

57 ratings

Epistolary essay filmmaking that ruminates on the failure of bodies, on how time and memory mark us, and on the power of creation and transformation to renew us.

3) Girl Stroke Boy (1971)

187 ratings

Smart and funny and ahead of its time  — even if some of its ideas might be dated by today's standards, it feels downright courageous and celebratory for 1971.

4) Behind the Door (1919)

425 ratings 

Animated by the same righteous vengeance that Quentin Tarantino deploys in his more recent works, and to similarly gruesome effect.

5) The Manor of Araucaria (1986)

662 ratings

Something like the sun-dappled gothic of Morgiana meets the psychoerotic dynamics of Teorema — but this cast of misfits isn't familial in any conventional sense, and they're way more interesting to boot.

Lots of more obscure films would qualify, but these are all in my top 40, so...

1) For the Plasma (2014), 203 IMDB ratings - 2 young women partaking in capital by observing the trees

2) \*Corpus Callosum (2002), 262 ratings - zoned out doing office work and chewing bubblegum

3) The Territory (1981), 299 ratings - trolling by way of cannibalism, waking up beside patches of snow

4) The Son of Joseph (2016) 909 ratings - ~~killing~~ finding a father?

5) Le Pont du Nord (1981) 1.4k ratings - mother-daughter bonding in Paris

6) The Falls (1980) 1.7k ratings - bird flu bonanza 

7) Buzzard (2014) 2.3k ratings - i hate myself

8) A Bride for Rip Van Winkle (2016) 2.3k ratings - depression

9) Trouble in Mind (1985) 2.5k ratings - RIP Kris Kristofferson 

10) Smithereens (1982) 2.7k ratings - hmm

1) The Nun (1966)

I fully agree with you on that one. It is absolutely a masterpiece and more people should see it.

2-4) Blood Wedding (1981), Carmen (1983), El amor brujo (1986)

The Flamenco trilogy by Carlos Saura. I am not really into dance movies, but these films are the exception. The first one, which is also my favorite, is just over an hour long and is unlike anything else I have ever seen.

5) Interrogation (1989)

One of those films you can't really recommend to anyone so I understand why it doesn't have a lot of ratings. It shows the extremes of human cruelty and violence.

6) The Pumpkin Eater (1964)

A British kitchen sink drama starring Mrs. Robinson and Mr. Beale. No idea why this one is forgotten to be honest.

7) This Man Must Die (1969)

I saw this one based on the title and I definitely wasn't disappointed.

8) Beauty and the Dogs (2017)

It is an independent Tunisian film. Has a similar vibe to Safdie films, i.e stressful as fuck.

9) Peppermint Frappe (1967)

Another one by Carlos Saura. A Hitchcockian thriller about a middle-aged man obsessed with his friend's wife.

10) Days of Heaven (2023)

This one came out last year and only has 260 votes for some reason. It's not a masterpiece or anything, but it's a pretty good film nonetheless.

1. *west side avenue* 2001 diaz (1.5k letterboxd views) — violence and its effects in a filipino american neighborhood 
2. *the general line / old and new* 1929 eisenstein (3.5k) — soviet industrialisation; has some of the most beautiful montage ive ever seen. this space could also share many lesser-seen vertov movies
3. *dont go breaking my heart* 2011 to (4.3k) — love triangle in contemporary hong kong. its really sweet and an amazing use of blocking, symbolism, and criticisms of. also directed by one of the hong kong action goats 
4. *intimacies* 2012 hamaguchi (1.4k) — actors rehearsing, performing, and then convening years after, a play. really poetic and beautiful and sad
5. *water and power* 1989 o'niell (1.7k) — the colonisation and industrialisation of california as told through visual and sound montage
6. *red army / PFLP declaration of world war* 1971 adachi, wakamatsu (1.9k) — revolutionary montage right here. eisensteinian, palestinian, a complete call to action, arms, and revolution
7. *i come with the rain* 2009 anh hung (1.9k) — american cop in southeast asia has to solve a complex murder. very francis bacon, very michael mann, very kiyoshi kurosawa, a soundtrack full of radiohead. its perfect
8. *the revenge: a visit from fate* 1997 kiyoshi kurosawa (430) — police detective takes revenge on a murder personal to him. if youve seen any kurosawa from the 90s, you know the energy this exudes already; deep nihilistic ressentiment
9. *ashkal: the tunisian investigation* 2022 chebbi (2.2k) — *cure* 1997 on immolation
10. *a rifle and a bag* 2020 hanes et al. (460) — chilling portrait of rural life in india, and the taboo of the means to resistance, even in family, in people who understand and agree, etc. melancholic but important movie

1. My engines fragile sound (2012) 

120 ratings 

A Portuguese film I stumbled upon on tubi. A weird mystery film about a nurse caring for a pregnant burn victim, who is drawn towards the victims attacker. 

2. Digging for belladonna  (2006) 

153 ratings

A German short film of 40 min in black and white reminiscent of gothic horror tales. 

3. Everything is terrible presents: the great satan  (2018) 

269 ratings 

A film that is hard to describe about the Christian satan told through thousands of intercut snippets of Christian propaganda films and YouTube clips. A true experience 

4. The wanting mare (2020) 

602 ratings 

A dream like film following a mysterious woman stuck on an island 

5. Black night (2005) 

633 ratings 

A French film set in a dark surrealist world, very much a noir mystery 

6. The mad room (1969) 

673 ratings 

An adult woman is caring for her two young siblings who were just released from a mental institution and have developed peculiar coping mechanisms. 

7. The blazing world (2022) 

772 ratings 

A young woman tries to find out the truth about her sisters drowning and is pulled into a surreal nightmare world. 

8. Scalpel (1977) 

918 ratings 

A cosmetic surgeon tries to steal his estranged daughter’s inheritance by altering the face of a strange woman to look like his daughter. When the daughter returns to her home, things go awry and the ending twist is well worthwhile. Heavily influenced by eyes without a face with a new spin. 

9. Idaho transfer (1973) 

1k ratings 

A slow sci fi film dealing with a group of people who invented a time travel machine to the past in order to escape the looming apocalypse of waning resources. 

10. Alison’s birthday 

1.3k ratings

Alison returns home for her 18th birthday, but doesn’t realise that she is at the centre of a ritual planned for decades by a cult. 

Honorable mentions

The trouble with being born (2020) 

Wild (2016)

Blood tea and red string (2006) 

Brother of sleep (1995) 

History of the occult (2020) 

The alchemists cookbook (2016)
